did_you_know.text: Did you know? The psalm’s title identifies it as a psalm of David, composed when he was fleeing from his son Absalom.
Did you know? David describes his distress by emphasizing the number of his enemies: “How numerous are my foes” and “Many are rising against me.”
Did you know? The enemies do not merely threaten David; they also claim that he has no deliverance from God. This portrays both external danger and spiritual doubt.
Did you know? David uses three images to describe the Lord’s help: the Lord is a “shield” around him, grants him “glory,” and lifts up his head.
Did you know? David describes a prayer that receives an answer: he calls to the Lord, and the answer comes, in the words of the psalm, “from his holy hill.”
Did you know? Even in a time of danger, David describes the natural cycle of resting and waking—“I lay down” and “I slept,” followed by “I awoke”—because he trusts that the Lord sustains him.
Did you know? The expression “many thousands of people” describes a vast crowd surrounding David on every side, yet he declares, “I will not be afraid.”
Did you know? David asks the Lord to rise and save him, using vivid imagery to describe the defeat of his enemies: striking them on the cheek and breaking the teeth of the wicked.
Did you know? The psalm’s conclusion broadens David’s personal request into a general declaration: deliverance belongs to the Lord, and his blessing rests on his people.
